subject.title: fix: normalize unsupported Anthropic inline images

question: Should Anthropic-specific byte normalization permanently live at the provider payload boundary through the optional AiTransportHost.normalizeAnthropicInlineContentBlocks capability?
rationale: The implementation is correct, but accepting it creates a durable published package-to-core seam; the competing fix instead changes the earlier shared sanitizer and has different ownership and cross-provider semantics.

options.title: Keep the provider host capability
options.body: Accept the optional hook so Anthropic owns its format allowlist at payload construction while OpenClaw core supplies byte conversion.

options.title: Adopt the shared sanitizer boundary
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102374 only if maintainers want normalization before provider selection and can prove every Anthropic-bound image traverses that sanitizer without unwanted sibling-provider effects.

recommendation.title: Keep the provider host capability
recommendation.body: Accept the optional hook so Anthropic owns its format allowlist at payload construction while OpenClaw core supplies byte conversion.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history ties the published AI host surface to Peter Steinberger, making them the best available decision owner for adding a permanent package capability.
